mentor.headline: A and B are eating your contests. The difficulty is not what stops you.
mentor.detail: Round 1117 finished at rank 4961, 1022 to 1132. A was accepted at +17 minutes and B at +63 — eighty minutes for two problems you can both solve on sight. D then fell at +114, so the ceiling is not the problem. C was a tree problem and it never got read. That is the entire 468 points: minutes on A and B, and a rooted-tree toolkit you do not yet have.

days.concept: A rooted tree is an array, not a diagram. Pick a root, build children lists, then produce one post-order with an explicit stack. After that every subtree question is a single accumulation over that order, and DSU answers the same questions when the edges arrive in no useful sequence.
days.watchFor: Every core problem today is a tree or a set-union problem, and the trap is identical each time: you will reach for recursion. Python's default limit kills 1676G and 1830A on the deep test, and the failure looks like a wrong answer rather than a crash. Write the explicit stack first, before any logic.

blocks.label: Mixed opener · technique withheld
blocks.note: Two problems from topics you have already covered, tags hidden. Name the technique in one line before you write anything. A wrong line here is the most useful thing this session records — it is the error that loses C in a real round.

problems.name: Right Left Wrong
problems.reveal: Pair the k-th L from the left with the k-th R from the right and take the prefix sum between them. Pairing outermost-first is optimal because those intervals nest, so every inner pair is counted by every outer one.

problems.name: Strange Birthday Party
problems.reveal: c is given non-decreasing, so the only gift worth buying is the cheapest unused one. Sort friends by k descending and hand out gifts 1, 2, 3 … to the largest k first; anyone left is paid c[k_i] directly. Greedy, not DP — the exchange argument is that swapping a gift toward a larger k never costs more.

blocks.label: Core · rooted trees and DSU
blocks.note: One representation, three questions. Build the children lists and the iterative post-order once, then notice how little changes between the first two problems. The third asks the same thing when the edges arrive unordered, which is what DSU is for.

problems.name: White-Black Balanced Subtrees
problems.why: Owed since day 21. It is also the exact shape of the C you never reached in Round 1117.
problems.reveal: One post-order pass. diff[v] = (+1 if white else -1) + sum of diff[child]; count the vertices where diff == 0. The parent array is given directly, so you can process vertices from n down to 2 without building an order at all.

problems.name: Copil Copac Draws Trees
problems.reveal: Root at 1, then pass[v] = pass[parent] + 1 if the edge to v appears earlier in the input than the edge to parent, else pass[parent]. The answer is the maximum pass. A single downward relaxation, not a search.

problems.name: News Distribution
problems.why: DSU has no solve above 1300 in your history. This is the cheapest possible entry to it.
problems.reveal: Union every user inside a group to the group's first member; the answer for a user is the size of its component. Union by size with path compression — no traversal anywhere, which is the point.

blocks.label: Owed upsolve
blocks.note: Third scheduling. It gets finished today or it gets dropped with a reason — re-planning it a fourth time is not an option.

problems.name: Arranging The Sheep
problems.reveal: Take the positions of the sheep, subtract the index from each to remove the width of the flock, then move everything to the median of those adjusted values. Sum of absolute deviations is minimised at the median — that is the whole problem.

blocks.label: Cold re-solve
blocks.note: Blank file, no notes, no old solution open. You solved this once with wrong submissions on the way, which is exactly why it is due.

problems.name: Omkar and Last Class of Math
problems.reveal: LCM(a, b) with a + b = n is minimised when a and b share the largest possible factor. Let d be the smallest divisor of n above 1; then a = n/d and b = n - n/d.

contest.title: Day 23 Contest · 20 Aug
contest.target: A inside 10 minutes and B inside 30. In Round 1117 they took 17 and 63, and that is the only reason C went unread. Nothing here is above your band, so a slow A is a self-inflicted loss tonight.
